content.text: Data effectively runs through end of 2025. I'll anchor the "last two years" to the last month with data (2025-12) and compute the two series over 2024-01 through 2025-12.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH hf AS (
  SELECT ca.descendant_concept_id AS cid
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 316139
),
hf_visits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT vo.visit_occurrence_id, vo.person_id, vo.visit_start_date, vo.visit_end_date
  FROM omop.visit_occurrence vo
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = vo.person_id
  WHERE vo.visit_concept_id IN (9201,262)
    AND (2026 - p.year_of_birth) >= 18
    AND vo.visit_occurrence_id IN (
      SELECT co.visit_occurrence_id FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
      WHERE co.condition_concept_id IN (SELECT cid FROM hf)
    )
)
SELECT FORMAT(visit_start_date,'yyyy-MM') AS ym, COUNT(*) AS admissions
FROM hf_visits
WHERE visit_start_date >= '2024-01-01' AND visit_start_date <= '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY FORMAT(visit_start_date,'yyyy-MM')
ORDER BY ym

content.text: The steep decline after 2024-12 is a data-completeness artifact (the extract tapers off through 2025), not a real trend — so I'll flag it. Now the 30-day readmission rate: for each HF admission, whether the same patient had another HF inpatient admission within 30 days of discharge.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH hf AS (
  SELECT ca.descendant_concept_id AS cid
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 316139
),
hf_visits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT vo.visit_occurrence_id, vo.person_id, vo.visit_start_date,
         COALESCE(vo.visit_end_date, vo.visit_start_date) AS visit_end_date
  FROM omop.visit_occurrence vo
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = vo.person_id
  WHERE vo.visit_concept_id IN (9201,262)
    AND (2026 - p.year_of_birth) >= 18
    AND vo.visit_occurrence_id IN (
      SELECT co.visit_occurrence_id FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
      WHERE co.condition_concept_id IN (SELECT cid FROM hf)
    )
),
idx AS (
  SELECT v.*,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM hf_visits n
      WHERE n.person_id = v.person_id
        AND n.visit_occurrence_id <> v.visit_occurrence_id
        AND n.visit_start_date > v.visit_end_date
        AND DATEDIFF(day, v.visit_end_date, n.visit_start_date) <= 30
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS readmit30
  FROM hf_visits v
)
SELECT FORMAT(visit_start_date,'yyyy-MM') AS ym,
       COUNT(*) AS index_admissions,
       SUM(readmit30) AS readmits,
       CAST(100.0*SUM(readmit30)/COUNT(*) AS DECIMAL(5,2)) AS readmit_rate_pct
FROM idx
WHERE visit_start_date >= '2024-01-01' AND visit_start_date <= '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY FORMAT(visit_start_date,'yyyy-MM')
ORDER BY ym

content.text: The readmission query timed out due to the correlated subquery. Let me rewrite it as a self-join with a precomputed monthly readmission flag, which the engine handles more efficiently.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH hf AS (
  SELECT ca.descendant_concept_id AS cid
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 316139
),
hf_visits AS (
  SELECT vo.visit_occurrence_id, vo.person_id, vo.visit_start_date,
         COALESCE(vo.visit_end_date, vo.visit_start_date) AS visit_end_date
  FROM omop.visit_occurrence vo
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = vo.person_id
  WHERE vo.visit_concept_id IN (9201,262)
    AND (2026 - p.year_of_birth) >= 18
    AND vo.visit_start_date >= '2023-06-01' AND vo.visit_start_date <= '2025-12-31'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
      WHERE co.visit_occurrence_id = vo.visit_occurrence_id
        AND co.condition_concept_id IN (SELECT cid FROM hf)
    )
),
ordered AS (
  SELECT v.*,
    LEAD(visit_start_date) OVER (PARTITION BY person_id ORDER BY visit_start_date) AS next_start
  FROM hf_visits v
)
SELECT FORMAT(visit_start_date,'yyyy-MM') AS ym,
       COUNT(*) AS index_admissions,
       SUM(CASE WHEN next_start IS NOT NULL AND DATEDIFF(day, visit_end_date, next_start) BETWEEN 0 AND 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS readmits,
       CAST(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN next_start IS NOT NULL AND DATEDIFF(day, visit_end_date, next_start) BETWEEN 0 AND 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*) AS DECIMAL(5,2)) AS readmit_rate_pct
FROM ordered
WHERE visit_start_date >= '2024-01-01' AND visit_start_date <= '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY FORMAT(visit_start_date,'yyyy-MM')
ORDER BY ym

content.text: I have both monthly series (2024-01 → 2025-12). Let me visualize them in one report.

arguments.title: Adult Heart Failure: Monthly Hospitalizations & 30-Day Readmissions
arguments.subtitle: OMOP CDM, inpatient/ER-inpatient visits with a heart-failure condition, adults ≥18, Jan 2024 – Dec 2025
arguments.summary:
Heart failure defined as SNOMED 316139 (Heart failure) plus all descendant concepts. An admission is an inpatient or ER-and-inpatient visit carrying an HF condition. 30-day readmission = the same patient's next HF admission starting within 30 days of the prior discharge.

**Key points**
- Monthly HF admissions were stable-to-rising through 2024, peaking at **1,366 in Dec 2024**.
- The steep fall from early 2025 onward (down to 31 in Dec 2025) is almost certainly a **data-completeness artifact** — the extract tapers off through 2025 — not a real clinical decline. Interpret 2025 volumes with caution.
- The **30-day readmission rate was remarkably flat, ~24–27%** across the whole period, with no sustained trend. Late-2025 dips reflect small denominators and truncated follow-up, not improvement.

panels.title: HF admissions per month
panels.caption: Admissions rose through 2024 (peak 1,366 in Dec 2024). The sharp 2025 decline is a data-completeness artifact as the extract tapers off, not a true drop in HF hospitalizations.

panels.title: 30-day HF readmission rate per month
panels.caption: Readmission rate held steady at ~24–27% with no sustained trend. The late-2025 dip (down to ~10-20%) reflects tiny denominators and truncated 30-day follow-up windows at the end of the data, not real improvement.

arguments.footer: Cohort: adults ≥18 at analysis; HF = SNOMED 316139 and descendants; visits = concept_id 9201 (Inpatient) or 262 (ER and Inpatient). Readmission uses the next HF admission per patient (LEAD over visit_start_date), counting a 0–30 day gap from prior discharge. The analysis window was anchored to the last month with data (Dec 2025); the 2025 volume decline reflects extract truncation, so trend claims should rest on the 2024 data and the flat readmission rate.

Here's what the two-year view shows for adults with heart failure (OMOP data, Jan 2024 – Dec 2025):

**Monthly hospitalizations**
- Stable-to-rising through 2024, peaking at **1,366 in Dec 2024**.
- Apparent collapse across 2025 (down to 31 by Dec 2025) is a **data-completeness artifact** — the extract tapers off — not a real decline. Don't read 2025 volumes as a clinical trend.

**30-day readmission rate**
- Essentially **flat at ~24–27%** the entire period, no sustained trend.
- Late-2025 dips (down to ~10–20%) come from tiny denominators and truncated 30-day follow-up at the end of the data, not genuine improvement.

Definitions: HF = SNOMED *Heart failure* (316139) + all descendants; admission = inpatient or ER-and-inpatient visit carrying an HF condition; readmission = the patient's next HF admission within 30 days of discharge; adults ≥18.
